title: The init wizard — what happens on screen
html:
English | Português (Brasil)

The init wizard — what happens on screen

Tutorial 01 showed the wizard in action. This page documents the mechanism — the guarantees the wizard gives and the ones you can demand from it.

The principle: never creates without asking

Bare golmet init is always interactive — it asks, shows the summary, and only creates on ENTER at the confirm. It is the kit's answer to the accident that motivated the rule: an init run in the wrong folder (the HOME, next to the kit's global installation) created a workspace mixed with the kit's own state. Hence: the init never creates at the HOME root, and scripts/CI require explicit flags (--org or --into <container>) with --yes — without a TTY and without flags, the init fails closed (exit 2, nothing written, the remediation cites the flags).

The guarantees at any step

The whole wizard runs in raw mode (the same arsenal as install), and the guarantees are transversal: esc/CTRL+C cancel everything, at any step — nothing is created before the final confirm. ← on empty text goes back to the previous step, with the typed value pre-echoed for editing; n at the confirm also goes back to editing (it does not cancel). Text fields accept UTF-8 (accents) and backspace erases the whole character — in raw mode the keyboard ESC reaches the program, something the console captures in cooked mode.

The recommended mode in practice

For those who prefer the fast path, the flags are the wizard as a command: golmet init --org (declares the org, creates the .gitignore, registers in the global catalog) and golmet init <produto> --into <container> (delivers the product in the org's declared versioning model). --yes skips confirmation with explicit flags. The full declaration of the paths is in FORMAT §2 and in the reference (commands.md).
